title: Stalkwise Tor bounds from perfection of a closed immersion pushforward
statement: Let $i:Z\to Y$ be a closed immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. Use the derived direct image [def-pc-derived-direct-image] and its structure-sheaf unit [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure]. Suppose $Ri_*\mathcal O_Z$ is perfect on $Y$ [def-pc-perfect-complex]. For each $z\in Z$, the module $\mathcal O_{Z,z}$ restricted along $i^\sharp_z:\mathcal O_{Y,i(z)}\to\mathcal O_{Z,z}$ has finite Tor dimension: there is $n\in\mathbb N$ such that for every $\mathcal O_{Y,i(z)}$-module $M$ and $j>n$, both $\operatorname{Tor}_j(\mathcal O_{Z,z},M)$ and $\operatorname{Tor}^{\prime}_j(\mathcal O_{Z,z},M)$ vanish. Here Tor is derived in the second tensor factor and Tor-prime in the first, exactly Mathlib CategoryTheory.Tor and CategoryTheory.Tor-prime; the two asserted bounds may be chosen independently.

source.place: Tag 0A9U; hypothesis translation in step 1 of lem-sc-smooth-proper-diagonal-tensor-formula

proof.text: Closed pushforward preserves cokernels by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-pushforward-cokernel]. Additivity gives preservation of finite colimits; it already preserves finite limits. The exact-functor comparison singleFunctorCompRightDerivedFunctorIso therefore identifies Ri_* of the derived structure unit with the single complex of the ordinary pushforward. The structure unit is definitionally O_Z[0].

For each source point x, unfold IsPerfect and choose U, K and the derived isomorphism from hperfect(i(x)). Map the inverse of the preceding derived-to-ordinary comparison through the derived restriction to U and compose with this isomorphism. Apply [lem-sc-strict-perfect-closed-pushforward-stalk-resolution] to this specified local model of the ordinary single pushforward to get a bounded projective resolution P of the restricted source stalk and a natural-number bound n.

Compute Tor-prime at j>n using ProjectiveResolution.isoLeftDerivedObj for tensorRight M. The degree-j term of the mapped resolution is zero because tensorRight M is additive and preserves zero objects. ShortComplex.exact_of_isZero_X₂ and HomologicalComplex.exactAt_iff_isZero_homology therefore give zero homology. Transport across the computation isomorphism. This proves the first bound for every test module M, using the same n.

The natural symmetry isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-tor-symmetry] transports the first bound to Tor-prime_j(M,B). BraidedCategory.tensorLeftIsoTensorRight B is an isomorphism of additive tensor functors. Derive its hom and inverse using NatTrans.leftDerived; leftDerived_comp and leftDerived_id show that these remain inverses. Its component at M identifies Tor_j(B,M) with Tor-prime_j(M,B), so transport vanishing again. The bound n from the first assertion also proves the second assertion.

lean.statement:
theorem perfectImmersion_stalkwiseTorBounds
    {Z Y : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ Y) [IsClosedImmersion i]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Z.toRingedSpace))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))]
    [∀ U : Y.Opens,
      HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace).over U))]
    (hperfect : Y.IsPerfect ((schemeDerivedDirectImage i).obj
      (𝟙_ (schemeDerivedCategory Z)))) :
    (∀ x : Z, ∃ n : ℕ,
      ∀ (M : ModuleCat.{u} (Y.presheaf.stalk (i x))) (j : ℕ), n < j →
        IsZero (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} (Y.presheaf.stalk (i x))) j).obj
          ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (i.stalkMap x).hom).obj
            (ModuleCat.of (Z.presheaf.stalk x) (Z.presheaf.stalk x)))).obj M)) ∧
    (∀ x : Z, ∃ n : ℕ,
      ∀ (M : ModuleCat.{u} (Y.presheaf.stalk (i x))) (j : ℕ), n < j →
        IsZero (((Tor (ModuleCat.{u} (Y.presheaf.stalk (i x))) j).obj
          ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (i.stalkMap x).hom).obj
            (ModuleCat.of (Z.presheaf.stalk x) (Z.presheaf.stalk x)))).obj M))
